title: Silent upgrade probe and rollback journal
content:
Context:
This is a lab-style journal for doing a low-risk "silent" upgrade of the private inference runtime/control-plane in on-prem and VPC installations. The idea: deploy new runtime artifacts side-by-side, exercise them with mirrored/ sampled traffic and offline comparisons, then promote only when quality/telemetry is indistinguishable. This doc captures probe sequences, terraform module notes, API compatibility checks, rollback triggers, and lessons learned from the Nov 2025 experiments.

High-level approach (summary):
- Deploy new control-plane and runtime pods to a shadow namespace (no production routing).
- Mirror 0.3-1% of production requests (sampled at the LB) to the shadow runtime for synchronous side-by-side compare (non-blocking for clients).
- Run synthetic workload generator (match production token distribution) against shadow cluster to exercise long-tail kernel paths and KV cache flows.
- Collect diffs: token-level divergences, latencies, memory/GPU footprint, kv-cache hit/miss behavior.
- Gating: define numeric thresholds for auto-fail (latency p95 > baseline*1.6 OR error-rate +0.75% absolute) and for promote (divergence rate < 0.05% on sampled prompts, telemetry within 10% on key metrics).
- If a gate trips, exercise automated rollback: scale down new runtime, revert infra artifacts, and drain shadow resources.

Environment definitions used in lab:
- prod-egress-lb (mirroring configured at LB layer)
- shadow-namespace: private-runtime-shadow-202511
- tf-state bucket: gs://redwood-pd-tfstate/prod (use separate state for shadow: prod-shadow-202511)
- image tags: runtime:2025.11.10-silent-probe, controlplane:2025.11.10-liteconfig

Terraform notes (module & state):
- We created a duplicate of the onprem.tf modules with suffix "-shadow" to avoid any drift with main state. Key change: provider aliasing + backend pointing to shadow state file.
- Avoid changing resource names that are referenced by customers (appliance bootstrap tokens, dns entries). Instead, create parallel resources (kube clusters, route53 hostnames with -shadow suffix) and use temporary ingress shim.
- Module checklist:
  - infra/networking: set mirror_headers = true, sampling_rate = 0.005 (0.5%)
  - infra/k8s: set replica overrides for shadow nodes (min 3, max 6) to exercise autoscale logic
  - infra/storage: enable ephemeral KV tracing flag = true (for debug tracing only)
- Tip: use terraform import to attach existing secrets into shadow namespace rather than creating duplicates; reduces secret sprawl. Document commands used in the runbook section.

API compatibility checks performed:
- Contract surface: inference v1 (text generation), chat v1, embeddings v1. New runtime introduces a structured-output change behind a feature-flag in chat endpoint that changes minor field name in the tool-calling payload.
- Approach: keep feature flag OFF in shadow runs except on a small synthetic set so we can validate transformation code path. Do not enable for any mirrored live traffic.
- Add an API compatibility harness to run a suite of ~200 representative requests (from production prompt corpus) through both old and new runtime and compute JSON diff metrics.

Observability + gating signals to collect:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end (API gateway -> runtime)
- Model-level token throughput: tokens/sec, downstream enqueue delays
- Error types: 5xx, model decode failures, tool-calling errors
- Resource: GPU util (per-card), CPU steal, OOM events, free memory
- KV cache: hit ratio per-key prefix, cold-start latency for cached sequences
- Quality: token divergence rate, n-gram overlap, BLEU/ROUGE-ish quick heuristics for structured outputs
- Cost proxies: token compute estimate, sustained GPU-hours for shadow runs

Gating thresholds used in experiment (initial values):
- Auto-fail: p95 latency > baseline*1.6 for more than 5 consecutive 1m buckets OR error-rate increase >= 0.75% absolute sustained over 3 minutes
- Promote-ready: sampled divergence rate < 0.05% across the production prompt sample (n=10k) AND p95 within 10% of baseline for 30 minutes
- Manual-review: divergence 0.05%-0.25% -> requires product/ML sign-off and targeted evals

Rollback mechanics (automated + manual):
- Automated rollback flow (observability webhook):
  1) Alert triggers to ops-runbook channel via PagerDuty automation hook.
  2) Runbook job: scale runtime-shadow deployment replicas to 0 with gracePeriod 120s.
  3) Revoke mirror route for LB -> remove mirroring rule (terraform apply against shadow networking module).
  4) Reassign sidecar feature-flags to previous stable commit if applicable.
  5) Persist telemetry snapshot to gs://redwood-pd-incident-archives/YYYYMMDD and tag in incident.
- Manual rollback extras: collect core dumps from the oldest failing pod, attach to jira PD-914, and open infra PR to revert any terraform changes if drift found.

Concrete run commands and snippets used in lab (examples):
- Create shadow tf workspace: terraform workspace new shadow-202511 && terraform workspace select shadow-202511
- Apply networking mirror rule (dry-run): terraform plan -var="mirror_rate=0.005" -target=module.networking.aws_lb_listener_rule.mirror
- Start request mirroring (LB level): curl -X POST "https://controlplane.local/api/admin/mirror" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"rate":0.005,"namespaces":["private-runtime-shadow-202511"]}'
- Snapshot telemetry: gsutil cp /tmp/telemetry-20251123.json gs://redwood-pd-incident-archives/20251123/telemetry-shadow.json

Experiment notes & timeline (laboratory log):
- 2025-11-12: Shadow infra spun up (3 shadow nodes). Initial smoke tests: ok.
- 2025-11-13: Began mirrored sampling at 0.1%. Observed slight increase in backend 5xx (~0.04% absolute) due to a missing decode-edge-case in new runtime. Reverted sampling to 0.02 and flagged issue.
- 2025-11-17: Fixed decode edge case (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/511). Regression test suite run. Re-enabled sampling to 0.5%.
- 2025-11-21: Noticed KV cache warm-up behaved poorly for sequences >1024 tokens; hit ratio dropped and p95 increased to baseline*1.4. Decided to increase shadow pool to 6 replicas to better match production pre-warm behavior.
- 2025-11-24: After kernel selection tweak and minor quantization profile change, divergence dropped to 0.032% on 10k-sample, p95 within 9%. Candidate considered promo-ready pending manual QA.
- 2025-11-26: Manual QA revealed structured-tool payload corner-case; feature-flag re-ordered. Promotion postponed.

Postmortem-style observations (lessons learned):
- Sampling at LB is easy but noisy; add deterministic shadow traffic (synthetic) that exercises long-tail sequences to reduce noise in divergence metrics.
- Shadows must be capacity-proportional to production for cache warm-up testing; tiny shadow pools understate cache pressure.
- Terraform pattern: prefer ephemeral shadow state directories rather than duplicating resource names. Importing shared secrets cut down friction.
- API compatibility harness (json-diff summary) was indispensable to spot tool-calling field renames before any client regression.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide on standard shadow sampling rate for future silent upgrades (0.5% default?)
- Add a scoreboard dashboard for divergence by prompt category to help triage which prompt classes fail more often
- Automate divergence alarms to Slack channel with 10-top example prompts (anonymized) when threshold exceeded
- Formalize a lightweight customer notification template when a silent upgrade enters manual-review state

Appendix: quick checklist for next run (operator checklist)
- [ ] Create shadow terraform workspace (note workspace name)
- [ ] Verify mirror header injection enabled (ops->lb team)
- [ ] Deploy runtime/controlplane images to shadow ns with -shadow tags
- [ ] Run the 10k prompt compatibility harness and save diffs
- [ ] Enable mirror at 0.2% for 30–60m and monitor gating metrics
- [ ] If stable, ramp to 1% for 2h and revisit gating
- [ ] If pass, schedule manual QA and customer-impact review before any promotion

References and links to artifacts used in this journal: linked in metadata above.

Notes to self: this approach reduces blast radius but is heavier on infra and observability. For larger customers (private appliance deployments) consider scheduling a short maintenance window and using a hybrid silent+canary approach where we promote to a small fraction of live clients after shadow validation.

End of journal entry for silent-upgrade-probe-2025-11
